questions.q: How does nn.DataParallel execute a forward pass across multiple GPUs?
options: It requires torchrun to launch multiple independent scripts
Within a single Python process, it splits the batch across GPUs, runs forward in separate threads, then gathers outputs back to one GPU
It trains each GPU on a completely different model architecture
It launches a separate OS process per GPU with its own model copy
questions.explain: DataParallel operates within one process: it scatters the batch across GPUs, runs the forward pass per-GPU in threads, and gathers the results back onto one GPU to compute the loss — all GIL-bound.

questions.q: What mechanism does DistributedDataParallel use to keep every process's model in sync after backward()?
options: An all-reduce operation that averages gradients across all processes so every copy applies an identical update
Each process randomly selects whether to apply its own gradients
A central parameter server that broadcasts updated weights to each process
DDP does not keep processes in sync; each trains an independent model
questions.explain: After each process computes gradients independently on its own data shard, DDP performs an all-reduce to average gradients across all processes, ensuring every model replica applies the same update.

questions.q: Why does DDP need a DistributedSampler instead of a plain shuffling DataLoader?
options: It replaces the need for init_process_group entirely
DistributedSampler makes training run on the CPU instead of the GPU
It is required only for debugging purposes and has no effect on correctness
It ensures each process (rank) receives a distinct, non-overlapping shard of the dataset instead of every process seeing the same data
questions.explain: Since each DDP process runs its own independent training loop, DistributedSampler partitions the dataset by rank and world_size so no two processes redundantly process the same samples.

questions.q: According to PyTorch's own guidance, which approach is generally recommended for multi-GPU training today, and why?
options: Neither — multi-GPU training should always use a third-party library instead
DataParallel, because it synchronizes gradients more precisely than DDP
DataParallel, because it requires the least code
DistributedDataParallel, because it avoids GIL contention and the scatter/gather overhead that limits DataParallel's scaling
questions.explain: PyTorch's documentation recommends DDP over DataParallel even on a single multi-GPU machine, since DDP's multi-process design avoids the single-process GIL bottleneck and repeated scatter/gather overhead.

questions.q: What is torchrun's role in a DDP training setup?
options: It replaces the need for a DistributedSampler
It launches one process per GPU and sets environment variables like RANK, LOCAL_RANK, and WORLD_SIZE that init_process_group reads
It compiles the model graph for faster execution
It automatically converts the model to mixed precision
questions.explain: torchrun is the launcher for distributed training: it starts the specified number of processes (e.g., one per GPU) and populates the rank/world-size environment variables that dist.init_process_group() relies on.
